newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Authority backs ICI, Auseon venture.
newsitem.headline: Authority backs ICI, Auseon venture.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Tuesday it would not intervene in a proposed joint venture between Australia's two PVC producers.
ICI Australia Ltd said last week it would combine its domestic vinyl and PVC business with Auseon, wholly owned by Geon Co of the U.S., to form a new joint venture.
ICI, 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc , said the new company Australian Vinyls Corp Ltd would be owned 62.6 percent by ICI and the balance by Auseon.
ACCC chairman Allan Fels said in a statement that information provided by the companies indicated there were significant imports of PVC to Australia.

The companies had told the Commission the venture would put their operations on a more even footing with larger competitors overseas, improve efficiency, boost output and lead to some import replacement.
"The recent changes in the plastics industry show that world scale production is possible without a loss of competition," Fels said.
"The ACCC has recognised that reduced tariffs and internationalisation have put pressure on domestic business to increase efficiency," he said.
ICI said last week the joint venture was expected to start production by the end of July.
